name: Appwrite
summary: Appwrite Cloud's Free plan freezes your project at its limits, and on Pro you can set a budget cap that stops extra usage charges.
free_tier: Appwrite Cloud has a Free plan with fixed resource limits that are shared across your projects. You can have one organization and 2 projects on the Free plan, and you cannot buy extra resources. The exact limits are on the pricing page.
over_free_tier: On the Free plan, your project freezes when it hits a limit and the Appwrite Console goes read-only. For example, API access is blocked when bandwidth runs out, function executions are turned off, and new user sign-ups are disabled. Service comes back if you upgrade, remove resources over the limit, or wait for the next billing cycle. On Pro, your project keeps running past the plan's limits, Appwrite buys extra resources automatically, and you pay for them.
hard_cap: Yes, on Pro. You can set a budget cap on your organization. Appwrite says budget caps limit the amount of automatic scaling and prevent unexpected bills. Appwrite stops buying extra resources when the cap is reached. For bandwidth, the docs say API access is then denied until you upgrade your plan or raise the cap. Other limits, once reached, turn off things like function executions, new user sign-ups, realtime subscriptions and file uploads until the billing period ends. The cap covers add-ons (the extra resources) only, not the plan's recurring fee. The docs do not say whether a budget cap is on by default.
how_to_cap: Open your organization's overview through the profile menu at the top right of the Appwrite Console.
Under Budget cap, turn the toggle on.
Set your budget cap amount in USD.
how_to_alert: Appwrite emails you when you reach 75% and 100% of your resource limits.
After you enable a budget cap, an email alert is sent at 75% of the cap by default.
To add more, go to the Billing tab and use Budget alerts. You can add up to three checkpoints.
never_capped: The recurring fee of your paid plan.
The docs do not say whether fixed-price items, such as dedicated database compute tiers, count toward the budget cap.
gotchas: Free plan projects with no development activity for 7 days in a row are paused automatically. Appwrite only says Console development activity keeps a project active. It does not say your app's own traffic counts, so do not rely on it.
Since June 29, 2026, Free projects that stay paused for 90 days are deleted with all their resources. Appwrite emails you first. Open the project in the Console to resume it.
Pro and Enterprise projects are not paused or deleted for inactivity.
When you hit a storage limit, uploads stay disabled across billing periods until your usage drops below the limit.
Without a budget cap, a Pro project keeps buying extra resources as long as usage grows.
